answers.how: Fitting the ball’s vertical trajectory gives an acceleration of about 552 px/s², so the scale is 9.8/552 m/px. The ball diameter is about 12.4 px.
The middle person is about 99 px tall. Using the gravity-derived scale of 9.8/552 m/px gives about 176 cm.
The passer measures about 85 px tall in the later upright frames. Converted using the gravity-derived scale.
The receiver measures about 100 px from head to feet in the initial upright frames. Converted using the gravity-derived scale.
At 0.00 s, the passer and receiver are approximately 245 px apart. Multiplying by 9.8/552 m/px gives 4.35 m.
At 1.00 s, the fitted ball velocity has components about 112 px/s horizontally and 162 px/s vertically. Its magnitude, converted with the gravity-derived scale, is about 3.50 m/s.
The ball travels about 123 px horizontally over 1.10 s, averaging about 112 px/s. Converted using 9.8/552 m/px.
